about.heading: Heritage, Passion & Local Soul
paragraphs: We are Cali Cultural Tours, born and raised in the heart of Cali. Since 2022, we've dedicated our lives to sharing the vibrant spirit of our home with the world.
Tourism isn't just our job; it's our bridge to global cultures. We believe that the best way to know a city is through its people and its food.
Cali is COOLtural. Let us show you why.

tours.title: Cali Street Food & Local Culture Walking Tour
tours.description: Eat your way through Cali's culinary traditions: taste crispy empanadas, aborrajados, refreshing lulada, and sweet cholado while learning about the city's rich history.
tours.highlight: A flavorful walking journey exploring the authentic street foods and neighborhood stories that define daily life in Cali.
tours.languages: Guides available in English, Spanish & Portuguese
tours.meeting_point: Main entrance of Teatro Municipal Enrique Buenaventura
included: Two food tastings at every main stop.
Three main culinary stations plus surprise local stops along the way.
not_included: Hotel pickup or drop-off (centrally located meeting point; private hotel pickup and drop-off is available as an optional add-on, including for large groups).
Third portions or extra food at the tasting stations.

itinerary.title: Teatro Municipal Enrique Buenaventura
itinerary.text: Meet your guide at the main entrance of the iconic Teatro Municipal Enrique Buenaventura.
itinerary.mapLabel: Open Meeting Point on Google Maps

itinerary.title: Traditional Baked Goods
itinerary.text: Start with a taste of Valle del Cauca's famous pastries. Enjoy warm pandebono, fluffy buñuelos, and sweet empanadas de cambray.

itinerary.title: Surprise Stops
itinerary.text: Walk at a very relaxed pace while your guide shares cultural insights and introduces you to off-the-beaten-path culinary secrets & hidden gems of the neighborhood.

itinerary.title: The Authentic Fritanga
itinerary.text: Dive into savory local favorites. Taste classic empanadas, pork-stuffed marranitas, hearty papas rellenas, and sweet-and-savory aborrajados.

itinerary.title: La Báscula (Local Spice Shop)
itinerary.text: Step into La Báscula, a hidden neighborhood gem specializing in global spices grown right here in Colombia, and enjoy a sweet tasting of caramelized Colombian cacao (cacao garrapiñado).

itinerary.title: Ekia Artesanías
itinerary.text: Browse handmade regional crafts with the chance to pick up authentic souvenirs, accompanied by a tasting of traditional regional candies and artisanal Colombian liqueurs.

itinerary.title: La Linterna Living Print Museum
itinerary.text: Visit La Linterna, a living lithographic print shop operating since 1934 where heritage wood and metal presses still roll by hand. Watch master printmakers craft Cali's iconic, bold cultural posters right in front of you.

itinerary.title: Tropical Refreshments
itinerary.text: After a slight incline at the end of our short 700-meter route, cool down with a delicious ice cream made from Colombia's exotic fruits.

notes: Preparation: Wear comfortable walking shoes and casual clothes. Sunscreen and a hat are recommended for the 9:30 AM, 12:30 PM, and 3:30 PM departures. We also offer a 6:00 PM evening version.
Dietary Needs: Please note that traditional Colombian street food heavily features meats and fried items, meaning strict vegetarian or vegan options are limited.

Taste authentic savory treats like marranitas, papas rellenas, and classic empanadas at local spots.
Enjoy a safe, leisurely 2-hour walk (700m) at a slow pace, ideal for families and senior travelers.

editorial_box.title: The Flavors of Valle del Cauca
editorial_box.text: Cali's street food reflects centuries of Afro-Colombian, Indigenous, and Andean traditions unique to Valle del Cauca. On this tour, you'll learn the story behind beloved regional classics like the Marranita (a crispy golden sphere of sweet ripe plantain stuffed with savory, crunchy pork chicharrón) and refreshing ancestral specialties like Champús: a traditional sweet-and-tangy drink crafted from lulo fruit, crushed corn, pineapple, panela syrup, cinnamon, and clove leaves.

faqs.question: Is street food safe to eat in Cali?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every vendor on our Cali Street Food Walking Tour is personally vetted by our local team for hygiene, ingredient freshness, and turnover. We only take you to trusted, high-traffic family stalls and bakeries where locals eat every day, so you can enjoy authentic flavors with complete peace of mind.

faqs.question: How much walking is involved in the Cali food tour?
faqs.answer: The entire route covers only about 700 meters (less than half a mile) spread evenly over 2 hours on mostly flat downtown sidewalks. We keep a relaxed, unhurried pace with frequent seated or shaded tasting breaks, making it comfortable for families with children and senior travelers.

faqs.question: Can solo travelers book this tour?
faqs.answer: Absolutely! Solo travelers are welcome and never face last-minute cancellations due to low group numbers. All departures are 100% guaranteed to run even for a single traveler.

faqs.question: Are vegetarian or vegan options available?
faqs.answer: Traditional Vallecaucano street snacks heavily rely on cheese (such as pandebono and aborrajados) and fried pork or beef fillings (such as marranitas and classic empanadas). While cheese-loving vegetarians can enjoy several stops, strict vegan options are very limited on this specific route.

cross_sell.heading: Complete your Cali Experience
cross_sell.subtitle: Continue discovering Cali's iconic viewpoints, colonial history, and world-famous salsa culture with our locally led experiences.

tours.title: Cali Exotic Fruit Tasting & Local Market Tour
tours.description: Discover the vibrant colors, aromas and flavors of southwestern Colombia with a guided walking tour through Galería Alameda market featuring exotic tropical fruit tastings.
tours.highlight: Taste over a dozen rare Pacific and Andean fruits, explore traditional medicinal herb stalls, and experience Cali's central culinary marketplace with a passionate local guide.
tours.languages: Guides available in English, Spanish & Portuguese
included: Premium tasting of 7+ exotic tropical fruits.
Pipilongo pepper and candied cacao tastings.
Guided route including the city mural, spice stalls, tamale factory, and souvenir area.
Guaranteed departure for every confirmed booking.
not_included: Hotel pickup or drop-off (centrally located meeting point).
Coffee bags, extra snacks, or souvenir purchases.

itinerary.title: Artesanias La Calenita
itinerary.text: Meet your friendly guide right in front of 'Artesanias La Calenita'.
itinerary.mapLabel: Open Meeting Point on Google Maps

itinerary.title: Chontaduro & Culture
itinerary.text: Next, taste the iconic chontaduro with honey and salt, followed by a stop to admire a colorful mural depicting Cali's cultural icons.

itinerary.title: Doña Tere & The Spices
itinerary.text: Enter the bustling market aisles to visit Doña Tere's corner. Taste pipilongo, a regional pepper with aphrodisiac properties, and walk through the aromatic spice stalls.

itinerary.title: The Exotic Fruit Rainbow
itinerary.text: We head straight to the market's vibrant fruit stalls. This is the core of your experience: you will taste more than 7 unique, tropical fruits while learning about their origins and flavors.

itinerary.title: Sweet & Savory Traditions
itinerary.text: Enjoy crunchy candied cacao (cacao garrapiñado) before heading to Las Delicias de Ara to see the fascinating inner workings of Cali's largest public tamale factory.

itinerary.title: Coffee & Souvenirs
itinerary.text: We conclude the easy 2-hour stroll by visiting a local coffee shop (perfect for buying Colombian beans) and exploring one of the city's most complete souvenir zones.

notes: Accessibility & Facilities: This is an easy, 2-hour walk on mostly flat surfaces. For your peace of mind, clean restrooms and an ATM are conveniently located along the route.
Guaranteed Departure: We never cancel on you. Whether you are a solo traveler or a family booking at the last minute, your tour is 100% guaranteed to operate.
Preparation: Bring comfortable walking shoes, a camera, and some local cash (COP) if you wish to buy coffee beans or souvenirs at the end of the tour.

highlights: Taste the Rainbow: The heart of our tour is a generous tasting of over 7 rare exotic fruits from the Andes and the Pacific coast.

Explore safely at a gentle, easy walking pace perfectly tailored for senior travelers and families (restrooms and ATMs available).
Book with absolute confidence: this tour features 100% guaranteed departures with no minimum group size.

discovery_grid.title: Exotic Fruits You Will Discover
discovery_grid.subtitle: From tart Andean citrus to sweet Pacific palm delicacies, here is a preview of the iconic Colombian fruits you can taste at Galeria Alameda (selection adapts to the freshest daily harvest):

items.name: Lulo
items.alt: Fresh Colombian Lulo fruit sliced open showing bright lime-green pulp
items.description: Bright orange outside with translucent lime-green pulp inside. Lulo bursts with a zesty, tangy flavor (like a cross between kiwi, lime, and rhubarb) and is the heart of Cali's beloved lulada drink.

items.name: Mangostino (Mangosteen)
items.alt: Deep purple Colombian mangosteen split open showing snowy white segments
items.description: Known across the tropics as the 'Queen of Fruits.' Beneath its deep purple rind lie delicate, snow-white segments with a velvety, honeyed flavor reminiscent of peach and strawberry.

items.name: Granadilla
items.alt: Golden Colombian granadilla cracked open revealing sweet translucent seeds
items.description: A smooth, golden cousin of passion fruit with zero sourness. Crack open its crisp shell to spoon out glossy, pearl-like seeds packed with gentle floral sweetness.

items.name: Chontaduro
items.alt: Traditional Cali chontaduro palm fruit served with honey and sea salt
items.description: Cali's iconic Pacific palm fruit, boiled until tender and traditionally enjoyed with a drizzle of golden honey and a pinch of salt. Its rich, creamy texture tastes like a warm blend of sweet potato and chestnut.

faqs.question: Are there restrooms during the Galeria Alameda tour?
faqs.answer: Yes. Clean, accessible restrooms are available right inside and along the Galeria Alameda route, and your guide will happily point them out whenever you need a stop.

faqs.question: Are the exotic fruits safe to eat?
faqs.answer: Yes, completely safe. We exclusively partner with trusted, long-standing fruit vendors inside Galeria Alameda who maintain high hygiene standards, wash all produce carefully, and serve only fresh, hand-picked seasonal fruit.

faqs.question: What is a chontaduro?
faqs.answer: Chontaduro (peach palm fruit) is one of Cali's most iconic regional foods, harvested mainly along Colombia's Pacific coast. It is boiled until soft and starchy, peeled, and served with honey and salt for a creamy, slightly nutty, sweet-and-savory bite packed with nutrients.

faqs.question: Is the Galeria Alameda tour suitable for seniors and solo travelers?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. The tour lasts 2 hours over flat, easy-to-walk market aisles at a relaxed pace tailored for families and older adults. All departures are 100% guaranteed to run with no minimum group size, making it ideal for solo travelers.

tours.title: Specialty Colombian Coffee Tasting Experience
tours.description: Learn to taste and appreciate specialty single-origin Colombian coffees in a sensory masterclass led by professional baristas in historic San Antonio.
tours.physical_level: Easy (seated experience, no walking, A/C room)
tours.languages: Guides available in English, Spanish & Portuguese
tours.highlight: Deepen your coffee knowledge through multiple brewing methods, fragrance notes, and comparative tastings of award-winning regional beans.
included: Learn everything about coffee: from bean to cup, flavor profiles, and brewing methods
not_included: Coffee beans or products to take home (available for purchase)
itinerary: Welcome & Introduction — meet at the designated spot; intro to the world of specialty coffee.
Choose Your Coffee — select your preferred flavor profile based on your taste preferences.
Preparation Demo — the barista prepares each coffee in front of you using different extraction methods.
Guided Tasting — taste, compare, and learn to identify flavor notes, acidity, body, and finish.
Q&A with the barista — ask about processes, regions, and how to recognize great coffee anywhere.
notes: You'll learn: what makes a coffee excellent, why Colombian coffee is world-famous, caffeine vs. over-roasting, flavor profiles, SCA scoring, processing methods (washed, honey, natural), and brewing methods (V60, Chemex, etc.). Don't be afraid to drink 2 cups straight: good coffee is actually healthy.

tours.title: Authentic Colombian Coffee Farm Day Trip from Cali
tours.description: Journey into the Andean mountains to an authentic working coffee estate, walk among coffee trees, learn harvesting and processing, and brew fresh coffee at the source.
tours.highlight: A full-day mountain retreat experiencing the authentic bean-to-cup coffee craft on a scenic family-run Andean farm.
tours.languages: Guides available in English, Spanish & Portuguese
tours.meeting_point: Pickup inside urban Cali (hotel, Airbnb, etc.)
included: Visit a family-run, non-commercial coffee farm
'Coffee collector' experience: pick your own coffee beans, from the tree, with your own hands
Guided local coffee tasting session with a professional barista
Stunning views from local viewpoint 'the balcony of the valley'
not_included: Traditional jeep (jeepeta) ride — available as add-on
Personal purchases, souvenirs, or additional food & drinks
itinerary: Scenic Drive to Sevilla (~3h) — morning departure through mountains and green valleys with a stop for traditional breakfast: arepas, huevos pericos, cheese, and tinto.
Coffee Plantation Experience — arrive at an active coffee farm. Walk through the plantation, learn about the crops, and pick your own coffee beans.
Bean to Cup — follow the complete process: harvesting, drying, roasting, and brewing. Understand the care and craft behind every cup.
Authentic Local Lunch — regional flavors of Valle del Cauca at a local restaurant. Vegetarian and vegan options available.
Guided Coffee Tasting — led by a local barista; taste different methods and discover the notes, aromas, and flavors that make Colombian coffee world-famous.
Balcón del Valle Viewpoint — panoramic views of Sevilla and its coffee-covered hills. Perfect for photos before heading back.
Return to Cali (~3h) — comfortable drive back through the mountains.
notes: Time breakdown: 3h to town · 20min to farm · 1h 20min at farm · 20min back to town for lunch · 1h lunch · 1h cupping · ~25min at the viewpoint · 3h back to Cali
Our destination, Sevilla, is a small town in the coffee region of Colombia. Expect lower temperatures than Cali.

tours.title: Bean-to-Bar Chocolate Farm Tour & Workshop
tours.description: Discover organic Colombian cacao, walk through cacao plantations, roast beans over an open fire, and handcraft your own artisan chocolate bar.
tours.languages: Guides available in English, Spanish & Portuguese
tours.meeting_point: Pickup inside urban Cali (hotel, Airbnb, etc.)
tours.discount: 10% cash COP discount · 5% USD/EUR cash discount
included: Your own DIY chocolate bar to take home
itinerary: Pickup in Cali
Scenic Drive (~1.5h)
Farm Arrival & Tour — cacao trees, pod harvesting demo, fermentation, and drying process.
Hands-On Chocolate Bar Workshop — Design and create your own chocolate bar using fresh cacao and flavorful toppings.
Tasting & Q&A — try local chocolate (from 90% cacao to a commercial chocolate bar) and learn about what really is chocolate.
Return to Cali — drop-off at your accommodation or agreed meeting point.
notes: ~1.5h drive from Cali. Kids and pets welcome (family & pet-friendly). Bring sunscreen and comfortable clothes and shoes.
We're going to a farm, insects are expected.
tours.highlight: Interactive bean-to-bar workshop where you harvest, roast, grind, and temper your own custom chocolate bar from fresh Colombian cacao.

tours.title: Cali Salsa Dancing Tour & Public Lesson
tours.description: Immerse yourself in Cali's world-famous salsa scene with a fun group public dance class followed by a visit to an iconic local salsa club.
tours.highlight: Experience Cali's rhythm firsthand: join a vibrant public salsa class with fellow dancers, then soak up the music and social atmosphere at a legendary salsa club.
tours.physical_level: Easy or moderate depending on your willingness to dance
tours.languages: Guides available in English, Spanish & Portuguese
tours.meeting_point: Trumpets monument at the Plazoleta Jairo Varela
included: Visit & explanation of the Niche Trumpets monument
Entry & tour of the Jairo Varela Museum
Visit a local vinyl records shop
Entry & tour of the Salsa Museum
Entry & 2-hour group salsa class at La Topa Tolondra
not_included: Transportation to and from the meeting point
itinerary: Pickup in Cali — 15–40 min transfer to the dance studio/venue.
Public Salsa Dance Class (60 min) — beginner-friendly group lesson taught by local professional instructors.
Social Salsa Club Visit (90–120 min) — enjoy live music or DJ vinyl sets, observe authentic caleño dancing, practice your steps, or enjoy a drink.
Return transfer to your hotel or accommodation.

tours.title: Cristo Rey Monument & Panoramic City Views Tour
tours.description: Visit the iconic 26-meter Cristo Rey statue overlooking the entire valley, explore the renovated ecological walkways, and take in the best panoramic viewpoints in Cali.
tours.highlight: Breathtaking 360-degree viewpoints over Cali and the Cauca Valley combined with cultural highlights and historic architecture.
tours.languages: Guides available in English, Spanish & Portuguese
itinerary: Cristo Rey — drive up the mountain to visit the iconic 26m statue (1,440 m altitude). Panoramic views of the city, the Cauca River, and the valley. Outdoor sculptures, lush vegetation, and local snack vendors. Discussion of the hill's spiritual importance and its role during Colombia's internal conflict.
Sebastián de Belalcázar — stop near the statue of Cali's Spanish founder. Additional city views and historical context about his controversial legacy and the pre-existing indigenous cultures.
Parque del Gato de Tejada — visit the famous cat sculpture and learn about its history, symbolism, and the local artist who created it.
Barrio San Antonio — charming colonial neighborhood known for craft shops, colorful streets, and a relaxed vibe. Walk through the park, enjoy city views, and visit the historic church.
Túnel Mundialista — Colombia's longest urban tunnel transformed with creative lighting and art; connects different parts of the city in a unique, modern way.
Loma de la Cruz — open-air craft market where you can find traditional Colombian crafts, jewelry, and local souvenirs.
notes: Our itinerary is a suggestion but we give you the benefit of fully customizable experiences. You may request modifications to suit your preferences.

tours.title: Km18 Cloud Forest & Hummingbirds Tour
tours.description: Travel to the mist-shrouded Western Andes cloud forest at Km 18 to observe dozens of brilliant hummingbirds up close at Finca Alejandría with a complimentary welcome coffee.
tours.highlight: Watch dozens of hummingbird species in extraordinary numbers and proximity at Finca Alejandría, nestled in the cool Andean cloud forest.
tours.physical_level: Easy (seating)(all ages) or moderate with optional mountain walk
tours.languages: Guides available in English, Spanish & Portuguese
itinerary: Pickup at your accommodation in Cali.
Scenic 1h Drive — mountain route into the western Andes (last stretch on an unpaved road).
1h 45min at the Paradise — dozens of hummingbirds at feeders, other forest species at banana feeders, photography opportunities, and relaxation in the mountain climate with welcome coffee.
15-min Local Dessert Stop — on the way back, as well as pet baby goats.
1h Drive Back — drop-off at your accommodation.
notes: Colombia has the highest number of hummingbird species in the world. Unlike zoos or aviaries, this paradise is completely open — birds arrive freely, offering an ethical and genuine wildlife experience.
Bring: light sweater or jacket (the cloud forest can be cool), comfortable shoes if you want to walk.

tours.title: Pance River & Waterfalls Relax Trip
tours.description: Escape Cali's heat and relax by the crystal-clear mountain streams and natural pools of Chorrera del Indio — a comfortable, low-effort nature getaway just minutes from the city.
tours.highlight: Refreshing mountain pools and waterfall views visible directly from the entrance area — perfect for a relaxing half-day escape without strenuous hiking.
tours.physical_level: Very Easy: paved paths and comfortable stairs down; optional 5-min walk to upper stream. The main waterfall is directly accessible from the arrival area.
tours.languages: Guides available in English, Spanish & Portuguese
not_included: Food or beverages (we can stop on the way if you want to purchase some)
itinerary: Pickup in Cali — 25–75 min transfer depending on your location (last stretch on an unpaved road).
Time at the Waterfall (90-120 min) — swim in natural pools, explore the main Chorrera del Indio waterfall, and hike to the hidden second waterfall (~5-min uphill climb, optional).
Return to Cali — 25-75 min transfer back.
notes: The main waterfall is visible from the parking. It is very accesible even for people with reduced mobility. The second waterfall is a short uphill climb and entirely optional.
Swimming and getting wet is entirely optional. You can enjoy the waterfall and pools without getting wet.
However if you want to get wet, bring: swimwear, towel, water shoes or hiking sandals, change of clothes, plastic bag to store wet items, eco-friendly repellent.
Please make sure to get dry before getting back in the car to avoid discomfort during the drive.

tours.title: Colombian Pacific Whale Watching Day Tour
tours.description: Witness majestic humpback whales breaching in the warm Pacific waters of Bahia Malaga during their annual migration from Antarctica (July through October).
tours.highlight: Up-close boat encounters with humpback mothers and calves in one of the world's most pristine tropical Pacific marine sanctuaries.
tours.physical_level: Moderate — long travel day; not suitable for people with reduced mobility or spine problems. Babies not permitted.
tours.languages: Guides available in English, Spanish & Portuguese
included: Fast boat to Bahía Málaga National Natural Park
1h whale watching on a boat with a local captain
Local lunch (seafood is typical, vegetarian and other meat options available)
itinerary: Pickup in Cali (early morning) — 3h transfer through the western Andes to Buenaventura.
Fast Boat on the Pacific Coast (1h) — board a speedboat from the tourist port toward Bahía Málaga Natural National Park.
Whale Watching Tour (1h) — on a boat with a local captain. Watch humpback whales leap, slap their tails, and, if lucky, spot calves. (warning: whales are wild animals, sightings are not guaranteed).
Free Time at the Beach (1h) — swim, relax, snack, or simply listen to the sound of the ocean on a local beach.
Return Boat to Port (1h) — back to Buenaventura.
Return to Cali (late afternoon) — 3h drive back, arriving at night.
notes: Season: July to October. Babies not permitted. Not suitable for people with reduced mobility or spine problems.

What to bring: clothing you can get wet with, light comfortable clothes + light waterproof jacket, sandals or water shoes, sunscreen and repellent, hat, seasickness pills (optional), waterproof phone case, reusable water bottle, light snacks or fruit.

tours.title: San Cipriano River Tubing & Natural Reserve Day Trip
tours.description: Ride the legendary motorcycle-powered 'brujitas' rail carts into the pristine Pacific rainforest, swim in crystal-clear emerald pools, and float down the San Cipriano river on giant inner tubes.
tours.type: Private day trip with vehicle + rail cart
tours.feature: Brujita rail cart ride, river tubing & emerald swimming pools
tours.highlight: Experience Colombia's most unusual ride: wooden platforms propelled along railway tracks into an untouched rainforest biodiversity sanctuary, followed by gentle river tubing in crystal-clear water.
tours.physical_level: Moderate: easy jungle walking, entering and floating down river currents, and climbing onto wooden rail platforms.
tours.meeting_point: Pickup directly at your hotel or accommodation in urban Cali (around 7:00 a.m. - 7:30 a.m.)
included: Round-trip 'brujita' railway cart transport into the reserve
All entrance fees and local community reserve permits
River tubing equipment (tubes and safety briefing)
Guided jungle walk to natural waterfalls and emerald swimming holes
Traditional Pacific lunch prepared by the local community
Bilingual local guide throughout the day
not_included: Alcoholic beverages or snacks outside the included lunch
Gratuities / tips for local guides and drivers
itinerary: 7:00 AM - 7:30 AM: Morning pickup at your accommodation in Cali and scenic 2-hour drive through the Western Andes towards Córdoba / Zaragoza along the Pacific highway.
9:30 AM: Board the famous 'brujitas' — wooden carts powered by motorcycles that glide along old railway tracks through lush tropical jungle into San Cipriano village.
10:15 AM: Guided nature walk along rainforest trails to explore hidden waterfalls, natural swimming holes, and the unique biodiversity of the Chocó biogeographic region.
11:30 AM: Relaxing river tubing adventure floating down the crystal-clear, emerald-turquoise currents of the San Cipriano River back towards the village.
1:30 PM: Traditional Afro-Colombian Pacific lunch (fresh local fish or chicken, coconut rice, fried plantains, and salad).
3:00 PM: Return trip on the brujitas back to the vehicle staging area.
3:45 PM - 5:30 PM: Scenic return drive to Cali, with drop-off directly at your accommodation.
notes: What to bring: Swimwear (worn under clothes), water shoes or secure strapped sandals (essential for walking on river rocks), quick-dry towel, change of dry clothes, waterproof phone case or dry bag, and eco-friendly insect repellent.
Please bring cash (Colombian Pesos) if you wish to purchase fresh juices, local artisanal sweets (like cocadas), or souvenirs, as card terminals do not work inside the rainforest reserve.
Weather in the Pacific rainforest can feature sudden tropical showers, which is part of the ecosystem's magic. The tour runs rain or shine.
